programme.title: What Would You Do?
programme.desc: Using hidden cameras, host John Quiñones observes and comments on how ordinary people behave when they are confronted with dilemmas that require them either to take action or to walk by and mind their own business. Various scenarios are created that force people to make split-second -- and often surprising -- decisions, and variations of the situation (such as changing the genders, races or clothing of the people involved) are often featured to see if different reactions are elicited. Examples of situations on the show include a waitress being harassed by her boss, and a drunken valet trying to park cars.

programme.desc: A 71-year-old man wakes in the middle of the night, gasping for air. Paramedics rush to save him, but it's all in vain: he's dead by the time they arrive. What caused his death?

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: Dr. G must figure out if a man died as a result of his infected stab wound or if his history of drug abuse was the culprit.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: Both natural disease and sport's injury are likely suspects in Eric Brody's death. But then Dr. G learns that he was treated with antibiotics for a spider bite prior to his death.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: Paramedics respond to a mother in distress: one of her infant twin girls hasn't woken up. By the time help arrives, it's too late. But there is no apparent cause of death.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: A hiker stumbles across a man's dead body in the woods. The victim's brother is convinced he was murdered. Dr. G must get to the bottom of this case. Was foul play really involved?

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: A hotel clerk calls 9-1-1 complaining of severe facial trauma, but he has no recollection of what happened and dies soon after. Police are counting on Dr. G to aid them in this investigation.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: Dr. G has a challenge on her hands: a victim's body spent days decaying before it was found, and decomposition could get in the way of her investigation.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: Dr. G suspects that someone is responsible for a vagrant's unusual death. She'll only discover the truth by finding answers to the strange events surrounding this curious case.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: Even with many leads, including an insulin overdose, a tooth infection and chronic lupus, the pieces don't add up in the case of a woman's death. Will Dr. G be able to uncover the truth?

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: An otherwise healthy child had been complaining of stomach pains. Could the medicine his mother had recently given him be to blame? Or could his death be from something more sinister?

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: All circumstances point to foul play in the case of a dead hunter and the police fear that a killer is on the loose. Dr. G must provide them with answers before there are more victims.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: In an unprecedented double autopsy, Dr. G is determined to find out who is accountable for these odd deaths and solve the mystery of a love triangle gone awry.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: Dr. G must decide if she can perform a successful autopsy without the deceased's organs. As she ponders the decision, we are given a rare glimpse into a different side of Dr. G's job.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: As each lead turns cold in a gruesome murder case, Dr. G worries justice may never be served. As the autopsy draws to a end, Dr. G uncovers a shocking clue that may solve this crime.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: A daughter wants to surprise her dad with breakfast in bed but finds him unresponsive. His family is convinced they know what killed him, but Dr. G must let the evidence speak for itself.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: A teacher excuses himself for a nap after dinner, but he never wakes up. The man has a complex medical history that leads Dr. G on a hunt for an explanation to his mysterious death.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: A woman fears the worst when her aunt stops answering her calls. When her greatest fear is confirmed, Dr. G must determine one thing: was this a fatal fall?

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: A woman is killed in a drunk driving accident. At first, her death seems to be an open-and-shut case, but Dr. G discovers clues that the woman may have played a key role in her own death.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: A mother of infant twins notices that her son is not breathing. EMTs attempt to revive him, but it's too late. Now, Dr. G must work fast to determine if the other twin's life is in danger.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: A florist meets with clients for an upcoming wedding, but she suddenly collapses to the floor. With no apparent cause of death, Dr. G worries that this case may go unsolved.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: When an infant dies under mysterious circumstances, the young parents are prime suspects. Dr. G discovers several clues that bolster the child abuse theory, but the case is not clear cut.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: Police make a grisly discovery: a woman's battered and dead body. With little evidence and no witnesses, Dr. G must identify the body and determine the cause of death to catch her killer.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: A neighbor hears odd sounds coming from the next apartment. When police arrive, they find a man bruised and dead. When all signs point to foul play, it's up to Dr. G to find proof of murder.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: It's up to Dr. G to determine if alcohol was to blame in a man's death or if there was a silent killer lurking in his body.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: Parents rush their baby to the hospital, but she tragically dies in her mother's arms. Now, Dr. G must help these devastated parents understand what happened.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: A train engineer panics when he spots a man lying on the tracks. He blows the whistle, but the train can't stop in time. It's up to Dr. G to piece together how Andy Santana died.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: It's up to Dr. G, along with the National Transportation Safety Board, to piece together how and why a plane crashed, leaving the pilot dead.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: Reed Baley is found unconscious the morning after his bachelor party. Now, it's up to Dr. G to determine if alcohol was to blame or if there was another cause of death.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: Authorities respond to a fire, only to find Carolyn Casey's body at the center of the blaze. With little evidence and no witnesses, Dr. G must find the cause of death to catch her killer.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: Leo Guzman falls off a ladder while painting a house. At first, his death seems to be an open-and-shut case but, as the autopsy unfolds, Dr. G believes there may be more to this case.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: A teen is eating breakfast when his dad starts stabbing himself. As the investigation unfolds, police begin to doubt the story. Dr. G must determine if this was a suicide or a murder.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: When Marie Allen visits her sister, she makes a gruesome discovery: the 49-year-old is dead on the couch. Now, it's up to Dr. G to figure out if this was an accident or something sinister.

programme.title: Dr. G: Medical Examiner
programme.desc: Dr. Farley discusses the bizarre case of a pregnant mother who suddenly dies. As the autopsy unfolds, Dr. Farley uncovers information that could have saved her and her unborn child's life.

programme.title: Total Wipeout
programme.desc: In this episode, the North of the country takes on the South in a battle to win the coveted trophy.

programme.title: Wipeout Australia
programme.desc: This week contestants on Wipeout Australia are bought undone by a seemingly simple obstacle on the Qualifier, the Slippery Stairs. It’s all in the name really, an innocent set of stairs, covered in Wipeout Crash cream. Its up the way and down the way for all and sundry. The lucky 12 that move through, battle it out with a giant toothbrush Sweeper. ‘Nat with the Tats’ and Renee ‘Lets get physical’ move through to the Dreadmill, flying the banner for the ladies. Look out for Scotty Six Toes at the Big Balls and get the ear plugs ready as you meet Herr Chris. It’s a colourful week with leotards, laughs and lots of ladies.

programme.title: Wipeout Australia
programme.desc: It’s Sitcom Central on Wipeout Australia with the Odd Couple, starring World’s Strongest Dwarf, David Clarke and Gentle Giant, Tim Watts. Once again the Big Balls deliver some spectacular moments with an Italian Chef being sliced and diced. Sacks are introduced at the Sweeper proving too much for some, but surprisingly helping the ladies to even things out as we go into a 50/50 male, female split in the Wipeout Zone.

programme.title: Wipeout Australia
programme.desc: Mesmerized by Bon Bon’s Belly Dancing, we catch up with our favourite Big Balls in the Qualifier. They dish out punishment to Australia’s very own female Jim Carrey and send Big Cat tamer Robbie into the pond. Goofy Goggles up the ante on the Dreadmill causing the Breakdancing Dad to create hilarious new moves. Golden Guns, Marisa battles it out for the ladies against Perfect Specimen, Seamus in the Wipeout Zone.

programme.title: Wipeout Australia
programme.desc: Wipeout Australia debunks the myth that only young, fit and funky people should go on game shows. This week we are forced to take notice of Demolition Dave, a 49 yr old South Australia man who thanks to some home training smashes the qualifier. For those lucky enough to survive the Fly Screen Sweeper it was Dizzy Dummy time. Emerging as the Dark Horse, Kobie Mulligan earned herself a shot in the Wipeout Zone, joined by a Strategist and Rubber Woman resulting in a bitter showdown.

programme.desc: From singing Pastors to Wookies, this week is jammed pack with Characters, who battle it out on the Qualifier with amusing attempts at the inconceivable Field Goal Swing. programme.title: Wipeout Australia
programme.desc: Fashion comes to Wipeout Australia as we meet Adam “God’s Gift” Marshall, a self styled Ad man who conquers the Qualifier. Other Catwalk moments include the Grandpa in his Red Speedos and a Rainbow Bright Personal Ad. If jumping a revolving arm while balancing on a pedestal above water isn’t enough for you then you’ll love this weeks Sweeper. Contestants are armed with Dodgeballs, to be deployed at each other, creating horrific hits and spectacular spills. The Dizzy Dummy claims its first victim as Dummy Tummy rejects a contestant and the Wipeout Zone becomes a battle of young and old.

programme.title: Wipeout Australia
programme.desc: It’s no doubt that the ‘Ball Crusher’ Sweeper is the star of tonight’s show. With a brother- sister team hanging by a thread and a three-way hurdle, this week’s Sweeper writes itself into the History books. Tonight is also the night we meet Buffman, a pint sized Superhero with a twitch and a photo finish at the Dizzy Dummy threatens extinction to a Rare Breed. A week of action packed Wipeouts with Latin Dancing lotharios, what more can you ask for? And for the kids, a Fairy Tale, Wipeout Style!

programme.title: Wipeout Australia
programme.desc: Showdowns don’t come more epic than this. Pro Wrestler Mikey takes on Wipeout Australias very own Tom Cruise. Its neck and neck through the qualifier which this week includes a real Mission Impossible, Dirty Balls. The trash talk is as fierce as the competition and continues to the Wipeout Zone with the winner taking not only the $20,000 but also the glory. Australia is also introduced to a new kind of “violent love”, the Fight Hug.

programme.title: Wipeout Australia
programme.desc: This week contestants on Wipeout Australia are bought undone by a seemingly simple obstacle on the Qualifier, the Slippery Stairs. It’s all in the name really, an innocent set of stairs, covered in Wipeout Crash cream. Its up the way and down the way for all and sundry. The lucky 12 that move through, battle it out with a giant toothbrush Sweeper. ‘Nat with the Tats’ and Renee ‘Lets get physical’ move through to the Dreadmill, flying the banner for the ladies. Look out for Scotty Six Toes at the Big Balls and get the ear plugs ready as you meet Herr Chris. It’s a colourful week with leotards, laughs and lots of ladies.

programme.title: Wipeout Australia
programme.desc: It’s Sitcom Central on Wipeout Australia with the Odd Couple, starring World’s Strongest Dwarf, David Clarke and Gentle Giant, Tim Watts. Once again the Big Balls deliver some spectacular moments with an Italian Chef being sliced and diced. Sacks are introduced at the Sweeper proving too much for some, but surprisingly helping the ladies to even things out as we go into a 50/50 male, female split in the Wipeout Zone.

programme.title: Wipeout Australia
programme.desc: Mesmerized by Bon Bon’s Belly Dancing, we catch up with our favourite Big Balls in the Qualifier. They dish out punishment to Australia’s very own female Jim Carrey and send Big Cat tamer Robbie into the pond. Goofy Goggles up the ante on the Dreadmill causing the Breakdancing Dad to create hilarious new moves. Golden Guns, Marisa battles it out for the ladies against Perfect Specimen, Seamus in the Wipeout Zone.

programme.title: Wipeout Australia
programme.desc: Wipeout Australia debunks the myth that only young, fit and funky people should go on game shows. This week we are forced to take notice of Demolition Dave, a 49 yr old South Australia man who thanks to some home training smashes the qualifier. For those lucky enough to survive the Fly Screen Sweeper it was Dizzy Dummy time. Emerging as the Dark Horse, Kobie Mulligan earned herself a shot in the Wipeout Zone, joined by a Strategist and Rubber Woman resulting in a bitter showdown.

programme.title: Ramsay's Kitchen Nightmares
programme.desc: The venue for tonight's first programme is La Lanterna in Letchworth, Hertfordshire. Twenty-eight-year-old owner and head chef Alex offers modern Italian cuisine, a taste of Little Italy in England's first garden city, and the restaurant is run by his best mate maitre dé Gavin, helped by his ex-air hostess girlfriend Emily. But Alex has no customers, cookers that don't work and an expensive menu that's about as authentically Italian as a spag bol.

programme.title: Ramsay's Kitchen Nightmares
programme.desc: The venue for tonight's second programme is D-Place in Chelmsford, Essex run by Mexican-born Israel and his English partner Tara. They've sunk ~£150,000 of their own money into their trendy café bar which offers a vast selection of fusion cuisine. In charge is Executive Chef Philippe, producing everything from all-day breakfasts to hoi sin noodles with an astounding lack of flair; the plastic food is dire and boomerangs back from the dining room as soon as it's cooked.

programme.title: Local Knowledge
programme.desc: Water quality is everything—and the Star brite - SeaSafe team is back at it for the second year in a row! Led by Cory Redwine, Conservation Director of Project SeaSafe, this is the 4th Annual Clean Water Collective and it’s bigger than ever. This time, we’re in Grant, Florida, where 4 million clams are being released into the Indian River Lagoon, paired with the planting of thousands of mangroves, oyster work by CCA and trash clean ups to help restore one of Florida’s most critical ecosystems. But it’s not just about hard work—it’s about connection. With local captains, fishing legends, and the Local Knowledge crew on hand, we hit the water to show why this place is worth fighting for. From clam drops by drone, to in-water mangrove planting, to monster snook catches, this is hands-on conservation at its best. This two-part series kicks off with action, heart, and the kind of hope only a healthy waterway can bring. Don’t miss Part 1—where conservation meets community and everyone gets their hands wet.

programme.title: Winchester Life

programme.title: Local Knowledge
programme.desc: Water quality is everything—and the Star brite - SeaSafe team is back at it for the second year in a row! Led by Cory Redwine, Conservation Director of Project SeaSafe, this is the 4th Annual Clean Water Collective and it’s bigger than ever. This time, we’re in Grant, Florida, where 4 million clams are being released into the Indian River Lagoon, paired with the planting of thousands of mangroves, oyster work by CCA and trash clean ups to help restore one of Florida’s most critical ecosystems. But it’s not just about hard work—it’s about connection. With local captains, fishing legends, and the Local Knowledge crew on hand, we hit the water to show why this place is worth fighting for. From clam drops by drone, to in-water mangrove planting, to monster snook catches, this is hands-on conservation at its best. This two-part series kicks off with action, heart, and the kind of hope only a healthy waterway can bring. Don’t miss Part 1—where conservation meets community and everyone gets their hands wet.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: A one-hour special that looks back at 2006, one of Dog's most tumultuous years, which has included the passing of Beth's father, Dog and Beth's wedding, the tragic death of Dog's daughter Barbara, and the sudden arrest of Dog, Tim, and Leland.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: It's been raining for days and the team is going a little stir crazy. Dog however has the cure--a good hunt. Maui has failed to appear on a drug charge and the team has just one lead.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: Dog and his team fight the war on ice - crystal methamphetamine - on many fronts. They appear on a special anti-drug float in a parade. Then they go after bail-jumping Pana, a convicted drug dealer.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: Beth designs a luxurious new office for the team and shows it off to Dog, but the bounty hunter is more interested in starting his hunt for Federico, who's been revoked for missing court dates and generally running amuck.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: Being hunted by the Dog is a lousy way to celebrate your birthday but that's exactly the spot that Robert finds himself in today. He's missed his court date, quit his job, and vacated his last known address.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: Dog's target for today was once an upstanding member of his community. Now with no home, no job and the law on his trail, this middle-aged exile from middle-class society is using the cold end of an ice pipe to soothe his troubled soul.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: Dog is hunting a man known as "The Godfather of Waikiki". The bond is small, Dog and Beth bailed him out as a courtesy, but now he is refusing to go to court. If Dog doesn't bring him in, it could cost him more than money.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter
programme.desc: Today the team isn't pulling any punches, literally or figuratively! In between tracking down a potentially dangerous ex-con facing a five year stretch in the big house, Leland is struggling to find time to train.

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter

programme.title: Dog the Bounty Hunter

programme.desc: Leland has a full plate of fugitives in Kona, and the whole family heads to the Big Island to help. They capture Clifford, who has a nasty habit of hitting his wife.

programme.title: The UnBelievable With Dan Aykroyd
programme.desc: Studying stories of revenge, such as the one about a man in Colorado that uses a Killdozer to settle a zoning dispute or another about an emperor who pickles his wife's lover; exploring vengeance seekers who take things too far.

programme.title: The UnBelievable With Dan Aykroyd
programme.desc: Toe wrestling; a competition between ugly pets; the origins of some schoolyard face-offs; exploring the world of strange games.

programme.title: The UnBelievable With Dan Aykroyd
programme.desc: A trip to the doctor is sure to cure any afflicted individual, but what happens when even the doctors are stunned by what they see?; from a family cursed with blue skin, to a girl allergic to the world's most unlimited resource and more.

programme.title: The UnBelievable With Dan Aykroyd
programme.desc: History is full of miracle cures, far-fetched products, and astonishing feats, but not all of them are legitimate; a miracle snake oil that cures all? A piece of the Brooklyn Bridge for sale? A marathon-winner who crosses the finish line without hardly breaking a sweat? These are the stories of some of history's most spectacular cons, each deception more unbelievable than the last.

programme.title: The UnBelievable With Dan Aykroyd
programme.desc: One-of-a-kind crimes are often met with one-of-a-kind punishments; like a pig whose bloody rampage lands itself in the courtroom, or a music enthusiast whose wall-rattling beats subject them to hours of classical symphonies.

programme.title: The UnBelievable With Dan Aykroyd
programme.desc: It is hard to believe that the beginnings of modern endoscopy are really all thanks to one professional sword-swallower; or that lack of sleep has some strange upsides; these are some unthinkable experiments.

programme.title: The UnBelievable With Dan Aykroyd
programme.desc: Uncover the wild beginnings behind ordinary objects, legendary figures, and even the sayings we use every day; why did Abraham Lincoln once step into the wrestling ring? How do million-dollar birds procreate? What's the story behind a dog that ignited an international conflict? These are the strangest origin tales you've never heard-and won't believe!

As the robbers became increasingly violent, pressure mounted to end their reign. With few leads, the FBI forced their own luck. The effort put them face to face with an armed and desperate fugitive.

programme.title: The FBI Files

As they learned that the killer had traveled extensively through the United States and Mexico, the murders became more frequent, and authorities had to cast a dragnet over an entire continent in an effort to catch him.

programme.title: The FBI Files

FBI agents noticed that one neighbor seemed to have the best rapport with the kidnapper. They began to question his level of involvement, but had to proceed carefully, knowing that he could be their only link to the missing woman.

programme.title: The FBI Files

As the hunt for the two men expanded, the FBI committed its resources to tracking down the suspects. The pursuit would take agents across six states to catch the killers before they struck again.

programme.title: The FBI Files

FBI agents and police are is in a deadly race to stop this murderous group with a dangerous cause.

programme.title: The FBI Files

programme.title: The FBI Files

programme.title: The FBI Files

programme.desc: Amid the cocaine wars of early 1980's Miami, three dead bodies led a multi-agency tactical squad to suspect that a group of cops might be involved in illegal drug busts. programme.title: Leaders with Francine Lacqua: The Podcast

From the midway, to the 4-H and baking competitions, to the mouthwatering fair food, Erika brings us the sights, sounds, tastes, and tradition of Maine’s oldest fair.

Tonight we explore Maine’s ‘Golden Road’ - the private road built originally to support paper companies; today a draw for people looking to get away from it all. We visit a “boom house” turned museum, meet locals who worked the timber drives along the Penobscot River, check out a company rescuing heritage timber from the bottom of a lake, and stop by the New England Outdoor Center (where, yes – we find a restaurant!).

programme.title: The Best of Chronicle: Main Streets and Back Roads
programme.desc: Mount Desert Island is a magnet for hikers, campers and sightseers. The Schoodic Peninsula – not so much. Surprising, because the two places have so much in common, including stunning coastal views and untamed forests. The difference: the Schoodic has no crowds. Tonight, we explore the peninsula, sampling local specialties like pickled wrinkles and dulse, revisit one of our favorite destinations, Wild Blueberry Land, and groove to Flash in the Pans – the hottest steel drum band in the state.

programme.desc: Chronicle's award-winning team brings you the stories of New England.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: A glimpse of unspoiled Maine for those “from away.” Tonight, Anthony Everett takes us up to Maine’s scenic St. George Peninsula. In Port Clyde, we get the history of a lighthouse saved by local volunteers and a labor of love. In Owls Head, Anthony takes to the skies in a vintage bi-plane and catches a ride in a 1929 Rolls Royce. We sample a taste of Africa in the middle of Rockland at Me Lon Togo, where the chef is also the musical entertainment. Finally, we spend time with a woman who is 102-years-young and still hauling lobsters.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: It’s a milestone year for WCVB (50 years) and Chronicle (40 years)! Tonight we meet others who are marking major milestones this year. The Boston Gay Men’s Chorus is celebrating 40 years on the scene; we talk to original members who recall the early days. Marking 100 years are family-owned businesses George’s Shoes in Jamaica Plain and Lopez the Florist in Dorchester (where Erika Tarantal gets a lesson in flower-arranging). Tune in for those milestone stories and more. Then stay tuned for a prime-time special, WCVB: 50 Years.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: A behind-the-scenes and inside-the-workshop journey of what goes into making music. We discover the precise and time-consuming task of making violins in Boston’s North End. From bass-making in Billerica to ancient Greek instruments in Lowell, we meet artisans and enthusiasts collecting, crafting, and restoring special instruments. We also get a glimpse at how music heals with therapy in Lawrence, and visit a church group in Brookline helping to launch a new generation of Black musicians in Roxbury.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: Scanned the real estate listings lately? Inventory is low, prices are sky-high, and some buyers are going to extreme lengths to lock in a purchase. Tonight Shayna Seymour surveys the market. We meet a Worcester mom who was forced to widen her search to find an affordable home, and families choosing to remodel rather than compete with other buyers. A local home inspector shares a few hints (and horror stories). Finally, Shayna gets a peek inside a $7 million mansion that offers a taste of the celebrity lifestyle.

programme.title: The Best of Chronicle: Main Streets and Back Roads
programme.desc: Water changes from a gray to a blue-green, flowers begin to bloom, and with restaurants reopening it can only mean one thing: it is spring on Martha’s Vineyard. Shayna Seymour takes a stroll near the Edgartown Harbor light, checks in at the Harbor View hotel, visits the Oak Bluffs Gingerbread Houses, and warms up with a bowl of conch chowder. She also tours the Martha’s Vineyard Museum where she learns about the little-known history of Black and Native American whaling captains.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: “Mightier” is a video game designed to help kids regulate their emotions, whose developers hope to treat kids with ADHD or autism. A new portable MRI – “The Swoop” – can make imaging easier for critically-ill patients. Nicole Estaphan meets clinicians, scientists, and tech pros developing and deploying advanced medical therapies -- right here in Massachusetts. She even finds a tech advancement not for humans, but for horses – a new way to treat equine asthma.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: Nicole Estaphan meets a local mom who has defied the odds and is alive 10 years after a diagnosis of Stage 4 lung cancer, thanks in part to targeted gene therapy.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: Nicole Estaphan meets a student/musician from the Berklee College of Music who was diagnosed with a tumor. Nicole also meets a young woman, one of the 1.5 million Americans with lupus, who underwent a groundbreaking new therapy that a local doctor says is a gamechanger. Tonight Nicole brings us these and other stories of patients and caregivers who are making a difference.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: As many as 25 million Americans live with rare, undiagnosed conditions. Tonight, Nicole Estaphan meets individuals living with rare diseases – and the clinicians and researchers who are determined to find answers.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: There is a national mental health crisis among young people, with girls and young women suffering in particular. Tonight one college student shares with Anthony Everett her personal story of struggling with severe depression and anxiety, and time spent in a crowded emergency room. A social worker who struggled to find help for her own daughter’s mental health crisis describes the critical shortage of care providers. Experts from Boston Children’s Hospital discuss the crisis-level need for more treatment options. Finally, we talk to experts who are finding new ways to connect with young people who need help.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: Tonight we take you along to see the lights, hear the music, and spread the joy of the season. Erika Tarantal meets a woman whose full-time job is spreading holiday cheer by wrapping big hotels and office buildings in festive decor.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: Tonight we take you along to see the lights, hear the music, and spread the joy of the season.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: Some are tiny – and some aren’t even visible to the naked eye. Tonight Erika Tarantal looks at how very small things can have a very big impact on our lives. Erika meets a researcher studying the brains of tiny ants, as well as two friends who co-founded a cosmetics company that uses microscopic algae as a main ingredient. Then, at the MWRA’s Deer Island treatment plant, Erika gets a lesson in how “bugs” (beneficial bacteria) are used to lay waste to…waste.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: In honor of Chronicle’s 40th anniversary, tonight we’re bringing you memorable moments from the “Main Streets and Back Roads of New England” – our show’s longest-running feature – and we’ll also hitch a ride in the Old Chevy for memories from “On the Road.” Prep for our Friday prime-time special with this road trip down memory lane.

programme.title: WCVB Chronicle
programme.desc: When it comes to wealth, transportation, property, health care – there are gaps in society. Tonight we talk to people who are working to bridge those gaps: An Ipswich farm provides low-cost access to fresh produce; a local man built an app to help people with physical disabilities navigate public spaces; a Lawrence nonprofit offers grants to businesses whose owners face barriers to capital. A look at the gaps that separate society, and ideas from individuals who are trying to close them.

programme.title: Time Machine
programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau visits geological wonders that have been shaped over time by water and ice. We go to the Grand Canyon, which is a treasure trove of earth's history. Then Philippe visits an ancient cave on the island of Curacao; a cave that was excavated by sea water thousands of years ago. We travel to Lake Michigan and discover how glaciers created the Great Lakes. Then we look into the future, and see if our planet will ever experience another ice age.

programme.title: Marine Restoration
programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau travels to Curacao and dives along the coral reefs to capture lionfish, an invasive species that's destroying the sea life in these waters. We visit the Chesapeake Bay to see what's being done to restore the oyster population. Then Philippe goes to Alaska and sees some areas that are still suffering from the Exxon-Valdez oil spill, which occurred over 25 years ago. Then we explore how the Mississippi River can be used to rebuild the disappearing wetlands in Louisiana.

programme.title: Time Machine
programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau visits geological wonders that have been shaped over time by water and ice. We go to the Grand Canyon, which is a treasure trove of earth's history. Then Philippe visits an ancient cave on the island of Curacao; a cave that was excavated by sea water thousands of years ago. We travel to Lake Michigan and discover how glaciers created the Great Lakes. Then we look into the future, and see if our planet will ever experience another ice age.

programme.title: Marine Restoration
programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau travels to Curacao and dives along the coral reefs to capture lionfish, an invasive species that's destroying the sea life in these waters. We visit the Chesapeake Bay to see what's being done to restore the oyster population. Then Philippe goes to Alaska and sees some areas that are still suffering from the Exxon-Valdez oil spill, which occurred over 25 years ago. Then we explore how the Mississippi River can be used to rebuild the disappearing wetlands in Louisiana.

programme.title: Siberian Tiger
programme.desc: This episode features a variety of animals found on land, and in the sea. Find out how the badger is able to dig tunnels up to 13 feet deep. And why the Siberian tiger is the largest cat in the world.

programme.title: Animals that Amaze
programme.desc: This episode features a variety of animals found on land, and in the sea. Find out why spider silk is 5 times stronger than steel. And how the vulture is able to digest some of the world's most deadly bacteria.

programme.title: Science On Fire
programme.desc: Join host Nick Uhas and his guests as they kindle our curiosity about the science behind fire. This week's experiments investigate how you can burn metal using only a 9 volt battery, what fire can teach us about calories, and why a little bit of sodium can cause a gigantic explosion.

programme.title: Like Button
programme.desc: When first presented with the like button (then dubbed "the awesome button") Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg had a simple response: "No." He worried that a quick thumbs up or down would discourage more meaningful online interaction. Eventually, his team changed his mind and transformed the world.

programme.title: America 250 Road Trip Itineraries
programme.desc: Photowalks host Jefferson Graham takes a road trip through American history. He's on a journey to take the best photos following America's founding in 1776, starting in Boston and ending in Washington, DC.

programme.title: Belgium: Castles, Cities & Countryside
programme.desc: Explore Belgium's beautiful cities, countryside and castles with Darley. Discover Dinant, Namur, Mons, Bastogne and Waterloo-meeting a top chef, kayaking to a castle, tasting Belgian beer and chocolate, and exploring powerful World War II history.

programme.title: Time Machine
programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau visits geological wonders that have been shaped over time by water and ice. We go to the Grand Canyon, which is a treasure trove of earth's history. Then Philippe visits an ancient cave on the island of Curacao; a cave that was excavated by sea water thousands of years ago. We travel to Lake Michigan and discover how glaciers created the Great Lakes. Then we look into the future, and see if our planet will ever experience another ice age.

programme.title: Marine Restoration
programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau travels to Curacao and dives along the coral reefs to capture lionfish, an invasive species that's destroying the sea life in these waters. We visit the Chesapeake Bay to see what's being done to restore the oyster population. Then Philippe goes to Alaska and sees some areas that are still suffering from the Exxon-Valdez oil spill, which occurred over 25 years ago. Then we explore how the Mississippi River can be used to rebuild the disappearing wetlands in Louisiana.

programme.title: Time Machine
programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau visits geological wonders that have been shaped over time by water and ice. We go to the Grand Canyon, which is a treasure trove of earth's history. Then Philippe visits an ancient cave on the island of Curacao; a cave that was excavated by sea water thousands of years ago. We travel to Lake Michigan and discover how glaciers created the Great Lakes. Then we look into the future, and see if our planet will ever experience another ice age.

programme.title: Marine Restoration
programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau travels to Curacao and dives along the coral reefs to capture lionfish, an invasive species that's destroying the sea life in these waters. We visit the Chesapeake Bay to see what's being done to restore the oyster population. Then Philippe goes to Alaska and sees some areas that are still suffering from the Exxon-Valdez oil spill, which occurred over 25 years ago. Then we explore how the Mississippi River can be used to rebuild the disappearing wetlands in Louisiana.

programme.title: Time Machine
programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau visits geological wonders that have been shaped over time by water and ice. We go to the Grand Canyon, which is a treasure trove of earth's history. Then Philippe visits an ancient cave on the island of Curacao; a cave that was excavated by sea water thousands of years ago. We travel to Lake Michigan and discover how glaciers created the Great Lakes. Then we look into the future, and see if our planet will ever experience another ice age.

programme.title: Marine Restoration
programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau travels to Curacao and dives along the coral reefs to capture lionfish, an invasive species that's destroying the sea life in these waters. We visit the Chesapeake Bay to see what's being done to restore the oyster population. Then Philippe goes to Alaska and sees some areas that are still suffering from the Exxon-Valdez oil spill, which occurred over 25 years ago. Then we explore how the Mississippi River can be used to rebuild the disappearing wetlands in Louisiana.

programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau visits geological wonders that have been shaped over time by water and ice. We go to the Grand Canyon, which is a treasure trove of earth's history. programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau travels to Curacao and dives along the coral reefs to capture lionfish, an invasive species that's destroying the sea life in these waters. We visit the Chesapeake Bay to see what's being done to restore the oyster population. Then Philippe goes to Alaska and sees some areas that are still suffering from the Exxon-Valdez oil spill, which occurred over 25 years ago. Then we explore how the Mississippi River can be used to rebuild the disappearing wetlands in Louisiana.

programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau visits geological wonders that have been shaped over time by water and ice. We go to the Grand Canyon, which is a treasure trove of earth's history. Then Philippe visits an ancient cave on the island of Curacao; a cave that was excavated by sea water thousands of years ago. We travel to Lake Michigan and discover how glaciers created the Great Lakes. Then we look into the future, and see if our planet will ever experience another ice age.

programme.title: Marine Restoration
programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau travels to Curacao and dives along the coral reefs to capture lionfish, an invasive species that's destroying the sea life in these waters. We visit the Chesapeake Bay to see what's being done to restore the oyster population. Then Philippe goes to Alaska and sees some areas that are still suffering from the Exxon-Valdez oil spill, which occurred over 25 years ago. Then we explore how the Mississippi River can be used to rebuild the disappearing wetlands in Louisiana.

programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau visits geological wonders that have been shaped over time by water and ice. We go to the Grand Canyon, which is a treasure trove of earth's history. Then Philippe visits an ancient cave on the island of Curacao; a cave that was excavated by sea water thousands of years ago. We visit the Chesapeake Bay to see what's being done to restore the oyster population. Then Philippe goes to Alaska and sees some areas that are still suffering from the Exxon-Valdez oil spill, which occurred over 25 years ago. Then we explore how the Mississippi River can be used to rebuild the disappearing wetlands in Louisiana.

programme.title: Time Machine
programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau visits geological wonders that have been shaped over time by water and ice. We go to the Grand Canyon, which is a treasure trove of earth's history. Then Philippe visits an ancient cave on the island of Curacao; a cave that was excavated by sea water thousands of years ago. We travel to Lake Michigan and discover how glaciers created the Great Lakes. Then we look into the future, and see if our planet will ever experience another ice age.

programme.title: Marine Restoration
programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau travels to Curacao and dives along the coral reefs to capture lionfish, an invasive species that's destroying the sea life in these waters. We visit the Chesapeake Bay to see what's being done to restore the oyster population. Then Philippe goes to Alaska and sees some areas that are still suffering from the Exxon-Valdez oil spill, which occurred over 25 years ago. Then we explore how the Mississippi River can be used to rebuild the disappearing wetlands in Louisiana.

programme.title: Time Machine
programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau visits geological wonders that have been shaped over time by water and ice. We go to the Grand Canyon, which is a treasure trove of earth's history. Then Philippe visits an ancient cave on the island of Curacao; a cave that was excavated by sea water thousands of years ago. We travel to Lake Michigan and discover how glaciers created the Great Lakes. Then we look into the future, and see if our planet will ever experience another ice age.

programme.title: Marine Restoration
programme.desc: Host Philippe Cousteau travels to Curacao and dives along the coral reefs to capture lionfish, an invasive species that's destroying the sea life in these waters. We visit the Chesapeake Bay to see what's being done to restore the oyster population. Then Philippe goes to Alaska and sees some areas that are still suffering from the Exxon-Valdez oil spill, which occurred over 25 years ago. Then we explore how the Mississippi River can be used to rebuild the disappearing wetlands in Louisiana.
